title: Responsible Use and Privacy
description: The Usage Policy, human review and disclosure, training and memory privacy, and connector and sharing risks.

cards.definition: For high-risk recommendations, a trained person must meaningfully review the output, with authority to change it, before it reaches anyone or drives a decision.
People who receive advice or are subject to a decision produced with AI must be clearly told AI was used, though naming Claude is not required.
Usage Policy areas needing extra safeguards: legal, medical, finance, credit, insurance, housing, employment, education, healthcare access, public benefits and legal status.
Usage Policy rules for every user and use, such as no illegal activity, compromising systems, weapons, inciting violence or hate, disinformation, fraud or privacy abuse.
On Free, Pro, and Max plans you choose whether your chats and coding sessions help train future models, and you can change it anytime in Privacy Settings.
Team, Enterprise, and API use fall under Commercial Terms, so the consumer training choice does not apply to them.
If you allow training on consumer plans, data retention extends to five years; if you decline, the existing 30-day period continues.
A ghost-icon chat outside a project that is not saved to memory or chat history and is never searched later; on Team and Enterprise it still follows org retention and exports.
Pausing keeps your memories but Claude stops using them and stops adding new ones; resetting permanently deletes all memories, including project memories.
By default Claude does not store topics like health, religion, or politics, and never saves items such as government ID or financial account numbers; an opt-in setting covers some topics.
Deleting a conversation does not remove memories generated from it, so those must be deleted individually in Settings > Memory.
Sharing a project gives members its knowledge and instructions at either permission level, but chats stay unshared, so keep sensitive files out of shared projects.
Treat code in someone else's published artifact like a file from an unknown sender, and check for shared storage before typing sensitive data into it.
Custom connectors are not verified by Anthropic, so connect only trusted servers, review requested permissions, limit scopes, and revoke access when needed.
Hidden instructions in a malicious server's output that try to make Claude take unintended actions; watch tool inputs and outputs even though Claude has protections.
Research can call connector tools automatically without approval, so disable any tools that can write or change data before running it.
Sharing a chat creates a frozen copy of the messages so far; later messages and attached files stay private, and unsharing then re-sharing refreshes it.
Anyone with a public chat link can view it without an account, so treat it as posted publicly; turning it off does not remove copies or screenshots already made.
Invite specific email addresses to view a chat snapshot; it is view-only, only the invited address works, and an unopened invite expires after 30 days.
On Team and Enterprise, chats can only be shared inside the organization, and admins can turn chat sharing off, review shared chats and revoke them.
On Team and Enterprise, an Owner or Primary Owner must first enable web search for the organization; members can then turn it on or off in each chat.
Admins have a separate toggle for anyone-with-the-link artifact sharing; switching it off also breaks existing public links, except artifacts individually allowed.
Manual asks before actions, Auto has Claude check each action for safety and uses more usage, and Skip does no automatic checks; permanent file deletion always needs explicit permission.
Owners can set an allowlist limiting Claude to named sites and a blocklist of sites it must never use, and Enterprise custom roles can grant the extension separately from Cowork.
